data.about: Seventy kilonewtons over seven metres, three times over — once as a point load between two pinned supports, once with one support on a roller, once spread out. The load never changes and neither do the vertical reactions. What changes is whether the supports will take a horizontal push at all: when they will not, the thrust has nowhere to go but inside the structure, and a tie appears. Switch the case and flip the structure between arch and cable.

steps.caption: EX 5 task 1: design a structure for each load case and draw its force diagram. The instruction that matters is “pay attention to the support conditions”
steps.title: The exercise

steps.caption: left: a seven-metre span and 70 kN, every time. Only the supports and the way the load is spread change between the three cases
steps.title: What is given

steps.caption: right: the load laid off. With everything vertical the reactions must add up to it, and by symmetry they share it equally
steps.title: The load line

steps.caption: left: pick how deep it goes and the members are drawn — up as an arch in compression, or down as a cable in tension. Right: the rays parallel to them meet at the pole, and the pole’s distance from the load line is the thrust
steps.title: Choose the shape

steps.caption: this is the question the support symbols answer. A pin can push back horizontally; a roller cannot. So in a) the thrust simply goes into the abutments — and in b) and c) it has nowhere external to go
steps.title: Where does the thrust go?

steps.caption: if the supports will not take the thrust, the structure has to take it itself: a member straight between the two supports, carrying exactly the thrust. An arch gets a tie in tension; a hanging cable gets a strut in compression
steps.title: The tie appears

steps.caption: left: green at the supports, and now visibly different between the cases — inclined in a), straight up in b) and c). Right: the same vectors closing the force polygon
steps.title: The reactions

steps.caption: drag the depth. A shallow structure needs a big thrust whichever case you are in; the only difference is who pays for it — the ground, or a tie you have to build and detail
steps.title: What it cost
